title: Inside King Tutankhamun’s Tomb, 104 Years After Its Discovery - Nautilus
gist: Paywall-truncated history piece marking 104 years since Howard Carter's team found King Tutankhamun's tomb. The visible text covers only the 1922 discovery: a downward step found while digging for Ramesses VI's tomb, in a valley that had already been heavily excavated.

insights.claim: On November 4, 1922, archaeologists led by Howard Carter cleared rubble that had built up about 3,000 years earlier and found a step leading down to Tutankhamun's tomb. They had been digging for the tomb of Ramesses VI.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Big finds can come from accident and persistence on ground everyone thought was exhausted.
insights.quote: They were digging for the tomb of Ramesses VI. What they found was a step leading downward.
insights.locator: The discovery of King Tutankhamun’s tomb

insights.claim: The Valley of the Kings had been extensively studied and excavated before 1922, yet Tutankhamun's tomb stayed hidden and relatively well protected from looters.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: A familiar parallel for investors: thoroughly picked-over territory can still hold overlooked value.
insights.quote: This wasn’t a pioneering expedition into unknown territory.

insights.claim: Tutankhamun's mask is described as perhaps the most famous archaeological find of all time.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: The tomb remains a major cultural asset and a draw for Egyptian tourism.
insights.quote: perhaps the most famous archaeological find of all time
